Coverage/data values are ILLUSTRATIVE (vision demo). FinCEN Alert, public domain (17 U.S.C. 105).

indicators.flag:
A customer with no history or background of using, exchanging, or otherwise interacting
with virtual currency attempts to exchange a high amount of fiat currency from an existing or
newly opened bank account for virtual currency or attempts to initiate high-value transfers to
VASPs.
indicators.red_flag: No-history customer initiates high-value fiat-to-crypto exchange / VASP transfer
indicators.rationale: A first-time-crypto customer pushing high-value fiat out of a new or existing bank account toward VASPs is fully observable on core account and wire/ACH rails, but no signal flags the no-history-to-high-VASP-transfer transition today.

build_logic.logic: Fire when a customer with no prior virtual-currency interaction history initiates high-value or escalating fiat transfers to known VASP counterparties from a recently opened or previously low-activity bank account within the window.
build_logic.source: core account ledger + outbound wire/ACH rail + VASP counterparty list
build_logic.route: Tier-1 alert → first-time-crypto outflow review gate

indicators.flag:
A customer mentions or expresses interest in an investment opportunity leveraging virtual
currency with significant returns that they were told about from a new contact who reached
out to them unsolicited online or through text message.
indicators.rationale: Detecting an unsolicited-contact investment pitch depends on customer-disclosed conversational context (chat/social-media origin) that the institution does not hold, so the data must be sourced before any signal is buildable.

indicators.flag:
A customer mentions that they were instructed by an individual who recently contacted them
to exchange fiat currency for virtual currency at a virtual currency kiosk and deposit the
virtual currency at an address supplied by the individual.
indicators.red_flag: Contact-directed fiat-to-kiosk conversion to a supplied crypto address
indicators.rationale: Kiosk-instruction-by-a-recent-contact is a verbal disclosure with no transaction footprint at the institution; the social/instruction context must be sourced externally before a detection rule can exist.

indicators.flag:
A customer appears distressed or anxious to access funds to meet demands or the timeline of
a virtual currency investment opportunity.
indicators.red_flag: Distress / urgency to meet a crypto-investment timeline
indicators.rationale: Customer distress or urgency is a branch/contact-center behavioral observation not captured in structured transaction data, so the affect signal must first be sourced into a structured field.

indicators.flag:
A customer uncharacteristically liquidates savings accounts prior to maturation, such as a
certificate of deposit, and then subsequently attempts to wire the liquidated fiat currency to a
VASP or to exchange them for virtual currency.
indicators.red_flag: Premature CD / savings liquidation feeding a VASP transfer
indicators.rationale: Early CD/savings liquidation followed by a wire to a VASP is fully reconstructable from deposit-product and wire records, but no signal chains the premature-liquidation event to the downstream VASP transfer.

build_logic.logic: Fire when a customer liquidates a savings or CD account before maturity (incurring an early-withdrawal penalty) and subsequently wires or exchanges the freed fiat to a VASP within the window.
build_logic.source: deposit-product ledger + early-withdrawal penalty feed + outbound wire rail + VASP counterparty list

indicators.flag:
A customer takes out a HELOC, home equity loan, or second mortgage and uses the proceeds
to purchase virtual currency or wires the proceeds to a VASP for the purchase of virtual
currency.
indicators.red_flag: Home-equity / second-mortgage proceeds funding crypto purchase
indicators.rationale: Loan-origination and outbound-wire records make HELOC/second-mortgage-proceeds-to-VASP partly observable, but linking a specific loan disbursement to the downstream crypto purchase needs the existing rule enhanced with proceeds-tracing.

indicators.flag:
A customer receives what appears to be a deposit of virtual currency from a virtual currency
address at or slightly above the amount that the customer previously transferred out of
their virtual currency account.  This deposit is then followed by outgoing transfers from the
customer in substantially larger amounts.
indicators.red_flag: Crypto return at/above prior outflow, then larger outflows
indicators.rationale: The small confidence-building return followed by larger outflows is a chain-analytics pattern; institutions see only partial VASP-exposure data, so the signal needs blockchain enrichment before it is buildable.

indicators.flag:
Accounts with large balances that are inactive or have limited activity begin to show constant,
uncharacteristic, sudden, abnormally frequent, or significant withdrawals of large amounts of
money being transferred to a VASP or being exchanged for virtual currency.
indicators.red_flag: Dormant high-balance account reactivated into VASP outflows
indicators.rationale: Dormant-account-to-active VASP outflow is detectable from balance and transfer history, but the existing dormancy-reactivation rule needs enhancement to specifically weight VASP-destined withdrawals.

indicators.flag:
A customer sends multiple electronic funds transfers (EFTs) or wire transfers to a VASP or
sends part of their available balance from an account or wallet they maintain with a VASP and
notes that the transaction is for “taxes,” “fees,” or “penalties.”
indicators.red_flag: VASP transfers memo-tagged taxes / fees / penalties
indicators.rationale: Repeated VASP transfers memo-tagged as taxes/fees/penalties are fully visible on EFT/wire rails including memo fields, yet no signal screens transfer memos for the extortion-style fee narrative.

build_logic.logic: Fire when a customer sends multiple EFTs or wire transfers to a VASP within the window where transaction memos match a taxes/fees/penalties keyword set, indicating coerced withdrawal-fee payments.
build_logic.source: EFT/wire rail with memo fields + VASP counterparty list + fee/tax/penalty keyword lexicon
build_logic.route: Tier-1 alert → coerced-fee transfer review gate

indicators.flag:
A customer with a short history of conducting several small-value EFTs to a VASP abruptly
stops sending EFTs and begins sending multiple high-value wire transfers to accounts of
holding companies, limited liability corporations, and individuals with which the customer
has no prior transaction history.
indicators.red_flag: Trial-EFT-to-high-value-wire pivot to no-relationship LLC / individual counterparties
indicators.rationale: The escalation from small trial EFTs to large wires toward never-before-seen LLC/individual counterparties is fully reconstructable from transfer history and counterparty records, but no signal models the trial-then-escalate pivot.

build_logic.logic: Fire when a customer with a short history of small-value VASP EFTs abruptly shifts to multiple high-value wires sent to holding-company, LLC, or individual counterparties having no prior transaction history within the window.
build_logic.source: EFT/wire rail + counterparty master + entity-type reference

indicators.flag:
System monitoring and logs show that a customer’s account is accessed repeatedly by unique
IP addresses, device IDs, or geographies inconsistent with prior access patterns.  Additionally,
logins to a customer’s online account at a VASP come from a variety of different device IDs
and names inconsistent with the customer’s typical logins.
indicators.red_flag: Anomalous IP / device / geo access including unfamiliar VASP logins
indicators.rationale: Anomalous IP/device/geo access is partly covered by existing account-takeover monitoring; correlating it with VASP-side login anomalies needs partial external signals, so enhance the current login-anomaly rule.

indicators.flag:
A customer mentions that they are transacting to invest in virtual currency using a service that
has a website or application with poor spelling or grammatical structure, dubious customer
testimonials, or a generally amateurish site design.
indicators.red_flag: Amateurish crypto-investment platform (poor spelling, dubious testimonials)
indicators.rationale: Judging a counterparty platform as amateurish relies on customer-disclosed site impressions the institution never collects, so the scam-site corpus must be sourced before any rule is feasible.

indicators.flag:
A customer mentions visiting a website or application that is purported to be associated
with a legitimate VASP or business involved in investing in virtual currency.  The website or
application shows warning signs such as a web address or domain name that is misspelled
in such a manner as to resemble that of another business, a recently registered web address
or domain name, no physical street address, international contact information, or contact
methods that include only chat or email.
indicators.red_flag: Look-alike / newly registered spoofed VASP domain, chat/email-only contact
indicators.rationale: Spoofed-domain and recently-registered-site signals require an external scam-domain / WHOIS corpus the institution does not maintain, so the data must be sourced before building a typosquat-detection rule.

indicators.flag:
A customer receives a large amount of virtual currency such as ether at an exchange,
subsequently converts the amount to a virtual currency with lower transaction fees such as
TRX, and then abruptly sends it out of the exchange.
indicators.red_flag: Receive-ether → convert to low-fee coin (TRX) → rapid off-exchange outflow
indicators.rationale: The receive-ether → convert-to-TRX → rapid-outflow laundering chain is a chain-analytics pattern observable only with partial VASP/blockchain exposure, so it needs chain enrichment before it is buildable.
